- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment shifts negative.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often underestimates rebound; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.7, -0.3, +0.7), model misaligns with sentiment rhythm; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
